_doc: What the checks may conclude from a manifest role (robot/body/checks/relations.py), only where the part's body definition (robot/**/<builder>.bom.yaml) does not say it: kind and spec.kind of a definition always win. Roles are the manifest's vocabulary, written by the builders; no part names. kind: printed | purchased | hardware | included | made | other (as the definition schema). classes: sets of roles the checks treat alike.

sleeve_set._doc: steel sleeves pressed into a printed part: hardware, but measured as part of that part (neighbours, bores, press)

shell._doc: body shells / covers: go on last; screened as neighbours only on request; their obstruction is reported apart

servo_case._doc: a servo's case (on the joint's parent link)

servo_output._doc: a servo's output wheel / horn / idler (on the joint's child link)

no_collision._doc: geometry that does not collide as a rigid body (glue, harness, sensor stack layers): left out of the motion sweeps

audit_skip._doc: left out of the standing overlap audit

solid_hardware._doc: hardware in the BOM, but measured as a solid part (neighbour, overlaps), not as a fastener

not_probed._doc: parts mount_check does not probe a screw against (no screw mates with a cell, its insulation or fins, a harness or glue)

geometry._doc: Thresholds of the derived relations (relations.py). touch_mm: a sleeve surface point counts as touching a part within this distance; mirror_tol_mm: largest box-face difference of an x-mirrored part pair.
